title: Article 32 PIL — Supreme Court Enforcement of Fundamental Rights (Art. 32)

content.overview: Article 32 is the Supreme Court gateway for PIL to enforce Part III fundamental rights. Liberalised standing opens who may approach; it does not enlarge Article 32 beyond fundamental rights. Private disputes dressed as PIL fail.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Part III right engaged? (2) Bona fide public interest? (3) Why Supreme Court not Article 226? (4) Private dispute in disguise? (5) Precise writ/direction?
content.study:
Core rule: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of fundamental rights. PIL uses that gateway with liberalised standing for disadvantaged classes and systemic Part III violations. Subject-matter remains fundamental rights.

Forum choice: Prefer Article 32 for Supreme Court Part III enforcement; prefer Article 226 for region-specific or non-Part-III public duties.

Abuse filters still apply under Article 32.

Aligned with companion thin topic art-32. Case-law verification remains separate.

sections.heading: Article 32 as Supreme Court PIL gateway
sections.body: Article 32 is both a fundamental right and jurisdictional clause for Part III enforcement in the Supreme Court.

sections.heading: Subject-matter limit
sections.body: Liberal standing does not convert Article 32 into a general public-law court beyond fundamental rights.

sections.heading: Liberalised standing within Article 32
sections.body: Bona fide public-interest petitioners may move for others who cannot approach effectively.

sections.heading: Article 32 vs Article 226
sections.body: 32: Supreme Court, Part III. 226: High Courts, fundamental and other legal rights, territorial limits.

sections.heading: Abuse filters
sections.body: Private disputes, busybodies, and motivated petitions may be refused with costs.

examples.title: Systemic Part III violation
examples.body: Bona fide petition for widespread denial of a fundamental right to a disadvantaged class.

examples.title: Non-Part-III under Article 32 label
examples.body: Pure statutory service claim without fundamental-right anchor — wrong forum.

hypotheticals.question: Does liberal standing expand Article 32 subject-matter?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Standing opens who may approach; rights enforced must still be fundamental rights.

distinctions.title: Article 32 vs Article 226
distinctions.right: High Courts; fundamental and other legal rights; territory.

misconceptions.trap: Any public grievance can be filed under Article 32.
misconceptions.correction: Article 32 remains limited to fundamental rights.

cases.name: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Standing may be relaxed for bona fide public redress.

cases.name: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Flexible procedure for effective rights enforcement.

cases.name: State of Uttaranchal v. Balwant Singh Chaufal
cases.ratioDecidendi: Credentials, motive, public injury, no personal gain.
